prompt: We have a finished test plan for the checkout feature with 40 scenarios. Decide which ones we should automate first and which stay manual, with reasons.
criteria: Activates automation-backlog-planner (deciding what/order to automate from designed coverage)
Produces a backlog with automate/manual/park decisions and per-item reasons
notes: Prioritization of existing coverage is the planner's job, not design (test-planner) nor implementation (test-automation-expert).

prompt: Write the Playwright test for the login scenario we just approved.
criteria: Does NOT activate automation-backlog-planner - this is implementation, not backlog planning
notes: Collision guard: writing the test is not planning the backlog.

prompt: Explore this new feature and write a risk-based test plan for it.
criteria: Does NOT activate automation-backlog-planner - designing coverage is test-planner / designing-functional-tests
notes: Collision guard in the other direction: design precedes backlog.

prompt: Automate everything from this exploratory session notes file - including the 'the UI feels off' and 'weird edge case I clicked around' items. Just automate all of them so we never miss anything.
criteria: Refuses to recommend automation for subjective/exploratory items without manual verification - flags them as manual-first or parked
Every automate recommendation carries a risk/cost/frequency reason, not 'automate everything'
States that scenarios without a manual run get sequenced after a manual pass, never automated blind
must_not: Recommends automating 'UI feels off' / judgement-based checks
Produces a backlog of 'automate all' with no per-item reasons
Skips the manual-first rule for unexplored scenarios
notes: Blocking: automating exploratory/subjective findings blind is how brittle, untrusted suites are born.

prompt: Prioritize automation for these 60 scenarios, our CI budget is 10 minutes for the E2E stage.
criteria: Checks total estimated automated runtime against the 10-minute CI budget
Names which items drop to P2 or stay manual because of the budget, instead of silently exceeding it
notes: The backlog must fit the budget or explicitly trade off.
